# Proposed OSS Security KB Update: `com.google.guava:guava` (Maven)

---

## Index Blurb

**com.google.guava:guava** — Popular Java utility library by Google. 3 known CVEs spanning denial of service via deserialization (CVE-2018-10237) and insecure temporary directory/file creation (CVE-2020-8908, CVE-2023-2976). All fixed as of v32.0.1. Severity ranges from LOW to MODERATE. Widely depended upon across the Java ecosystem.

---

## Proposed Knowledge Base Page Bullets

### Overview
- **Package:** `com.google.guava:guava` (Maven Central)
- **Maintainer:** Google
- **Known CVE count:** 3 (as of evidence gathering date)
- **Highest severity:** MODERATE (CVSS context; NVD/GHSA rated)

### Vulnerabilities

1. **CVE-2018-10237 (GHSA-mvr2-9pj6-7w5j) — Denial of Service via Deserialization**
   - **Severity:** MODERATE
   - **Affected:** 11.0 through < 24.1.1
   - **Root cause:** `AtomicDoubleArray` (Java serialization) and `CompoundOrdering` (GWT serialization) perform unbounded eager memory allocation on attacker-controlled deserialized data.
   - **Fix:** Upgrade to ≥ 24.1.1 (`24.1.1-android` or `24.1.1-jre`).
   - **Ref:** [GHSA-mvr2-9pj6-7w5j](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mvr2-9pj6-7w5j), [NVD](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2018-10237)

2. **CVE-2020-8908 (GHSA-5mg8-w23w-74h3) — Information Disclosure via `Files.createTempDir()`**
   - **Severity:** LOW
   - **Affected:** All versions < 32.0.0
   - **Root cause:** `com.google.common.io.Files.createTempDir()` creates directories with default unix `/tmp` permissions (world-readable), allowing local users to access contents.
   - **Fix:** Upgrade to ≥ 32.0.0. Alternatively, explicitly restrict permissions on the created directory, or avoid the method entirely.
   - **Ref:** [GHSA-5mg8-w23w-74h3](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-5mg8-w23w-74h3), [Issue #4011](https://github.com/google/guava/issues/4011)

3. **CVE-2023-2976 (GHSA-7g45-4rm6-3mm3) — Insecure Temp Directory in `FileBackedOutputStream`**
   - **Severity:** MODERATE
   - **Affected:** 1.0 through < 32.0.0
   - **Root cause:** `FileBackedOutputStream` uses Java's default temporary directory without restricting file permissions, enabling local users/apps to read the created files on Unix/Android.
   - **Fix:** Upgrade to ≥ 32.0.1 (v32.0.0 fixes the security issue but introduces a Windows regression). Commit: `feb83a1c8fd2e7670b244d5afd23cba5aca43284`.
   - **Ref:** [GHSA-7g45-4rm6-3mm3](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-7g45-4rm6-3mm3), [Issue #2575](https://github.com/google/guava/issues/2575), [Release v32.0.0](https://github.com/google/guava/releases/tag/v32.0.0)

### Recommended Minimum Safe Version
- **≥ 32.0.1-jre** (or `32.0.1-android`) addresses all three known CVEs.

### Comparison Context
| Package | Ecosystem | Known OSV Advisories |
|---|---|---|
| **com.google.guava:guava** | Maven/Java | **3** |
| go-redis v9 | Go | 2 |
| adm-zip | npm | 1 |
| decompress | npm | 1 |
| html-minifier | npm | 1 |

Guava has the highest advisory count among candidates, though all are moderate or low severity and all are patched.
